transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. 

I came in mostly because... well, my eating has gotten all turned around for months now. It's probably nothing major, but some days I just sort of pick at a piece of toast and have my coffee, and that's really it. But then—and this is a little embarrassing to admit—other days I'll find myself just standing in the bakery aisle at the grocery store, buying all these sweets. And I don't even really enjoy them, to be honest. 

It's silly, I know. I just... I hope it's okay that I came in to talk about it. Is that the sort of thing I should be here for?
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Oh, um... well, I haven't really been keeping strict track on a scale, I hope that's okay. But like I was just saying about my eating being all turned around for months... with just picking at toast some days and then getting all those sweets on others... I think my weight has been going up and down a little bit because of it. My clothes just fit a bit differently depending on the week. 

I'm sorry I don't have an exact number for you. I hope I'm giving you the right information... does that make sense, with how my eating has been?
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating when you're buying and consuming all those sweets?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say I'm completely out of control. I mean, I know I'm putting them in the cart. It's just... I guess I just get a little carried away sometimes? 

It's really not as bad as it probably sounds, I promise. I just, you know, I'm at the store and I see them, and... well, I just buy them. But I can always stop myself if I really need to. I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible. I know I should have better willpower at my age. Does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you feel guilty after eating those sweets?

Guilty? Oh... um, well, no, not exactly. I mean, I know I probably shouldn't be eating them, but... I don't really sit there and beat myself up over it. It's more just... I feel a little silly about the whole thing, I guess? 

I hope that doesn't make it sound like I don't care about my health. I really do care, I promise. I just don't get that terrible guilty feeling afterwards. Is it a bad thing that I don't feel guilty? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer.
Do you ever eat a large amount of sweets in a short period of time?

Oh, goodness, no... um, I don't think I do that. I mean, I might have a few things over the course of the whole day, but I definitely don't sit down and eat a huge amount all at once. 

I just sort of... space it out, you know? Just a little nibble here and there. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just gorging myself or anything like that. I really try to be good about not overdoing it in one sitting. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how it happens.
Do you usually buy or eat those sweets when you're feeling stressed or upset?

Oh, um... stressed? No, I don't really think so. I mean, I try to keep a pretty even keel, you know? I definitely don't think I'm reaching for them just because I'm having a bad day or feeling upset. 

It's more just... well, they just taste nice, I suppose. I wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, eating my feelings or anything like that. I really do try to handle my stress much better than that. Does that make sense? I hope that's helpful... I just haven't really noticed a connection like that, but I can certainly try to pay more attention to it if you want me to!
Do you think your mood has any influence on your decision to buy or eat sweets?

My mood? Oh, um... no, I really don't believe so. I mean, I try very hard not to let my emotions control things like that, you know? It's really just... well, just having a little treat because it tastes nice, not because I'm feeling down or anything. 

I know a lot of people might eat when they're sad, but I really try to be good about that. I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that I don't really see a connection there?
Do you feel like you're eating out of habit or because you're actually hungry when you have those days where you just pick at a piece of toast?

Oh, um... well, it's... it's a little bit of both, I suppose. I mean, some days I just don't feel like eating much, so I'll just have a little toast and coffee. I hope that's not too terrible? I just try to listen to my body, you know?

But... well, honestly, I think I came in because my eating has just gotten all turned around for months now. Like I said, some days it's just picking at toast, but then... well, other days I find myself standing in the bakery aisle buying sweets that I don't even really enjoy. I know that sounds silly, and I really don't want you to think I'm completely out of control. It's just... confusing, I guess. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay... I just want to be a good patient and give you the full picture, even if it's a little embarrassing.
Do you think your eating habits would change if you were in a different emotional state?

Oh, um... a different emotional state? I'm... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I mean, I really try to keep things steady, like I said. I wouldn't want to think that my emotions are dictating everything I do. 

I suppose... well, maybe if I felt a bit more energetic, I might cook a proper meal instead of just having toast? But I don't really know if the sweets part would change. I just... I haven't really thought about it like that. I hope that's an okay answer? I'm sorry I don't have a clearer picture for you on that one, I just try to take it one day at a time, you know? Is that what you meant?
Do you often find yourself not really wanting to eat because you're just not interested in food?

Oh, um... yes, I think so. Like I was mentioning just a little bit ago, my eating has just been all turned around for months now. So on those days where I'm just picking at the toast and coffee, it really is just because I don't have any interest in a full meal. Food just doesn't seem appealing at all on those days. 

And then, you know, it flips to the other extreme where I end up in the bakery aisle buying those sweets I don't even really want... like I said before. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself a little? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. I really do try to eat properly, I promise, it's just hard when the desire for it just isn't there. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.
Do you think your eating habits would be different if you were feeling happier?

Oh, um... isn't that sort of like what you were asking just a minute ago? About being in a different emotional state? I'm so sorry if I didn't explain myself well the first time... I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. 

But honestly, I'm just... I'm still not entirely sure. I suppose if I were happier, maybe I'd have more of a drive to cook a real dinner instead of just relying on the toast? But I try not to let my mood dictate everything, I really do try to keep things normal and be good about it. I hope it's alright that I don't have a more definitive answer for you... I'm really trying my best to figure it all out, I promise. Is that okay?
Do you often feel like you're not hungry when you're only picking at a piece of toast?

Oh, um... yes, I think you're asking about the same thing again? I'm so sorry, I really hope I'm not frustrating you by not being clear enough. I'm trying to be helpful, I promise.

But yes, when I'm just having the toast, it's really because I'm just not hungry at all. Like I mentioned, my eating has been all turned around for months now... I came in because of it, really. Some days I just pick at the toast and coffee because I have absolutely no appetite, and then other days, like I said, I'm in the bakery aisle buying those sweets I don't even really enjoy. I try to be good and eat normally, I really do, it's just... it's been so unpredictable. Does that answer your question better? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Do you often go for several days at a time where you're just not interested in eating?

Oh, um... yes, I think that's what I've been trying to say. I'm so sorry, I feel like I keep repeating myself and I really don't want to waste your time. I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up again. 

But yes, like I mentioned when I first came in, my eating has just been all turned around for months now. So, yes, there are stretches where I just have the toast and coffee for a few days because I'm just not interested in food. And then, you know, it flips and I'm buying those sweets I don't even really like. I'm really trying to get a handle on it, I promise. I know it's not the best way to eat, but I'm doing my best to be good about it when I can. Is that what you were asking? I hope I'm making sense.

Oh, dear... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm making this so difficult for you, and I really don't mean to. I know you're just trying to understand, and I appreciate your patience with me so much. 

I guess... well, I'm not entirely sure if there's a difference between the two? When I just have the toast, it's... I don't feel a rumble in my stomach, and I don't really have any desire to eat, either. It's just sort of a blank feeling. I hope that's an okay answer... I know it's probably frustrating when I can't be more specific. I'm really trying to pay better attention to these things, I promise. Am I giving you the right kind of information?

Oh... um, I'm not really sure about that. I'm sorry, I wish I had a better answer for you. I don't really know if stress is what's causing it. I mean, I suppose everyone feels a little overwhelmed sometimes, right? But I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. I just know that my appetite is all over the place. I hope that's okay to say... I'm really trying to be helpful, I promise. Did I answer that right, or did you mean something else?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself again, and I really don't want to be a bother. You're being so kind to ask.

I know I shouldn't, and I'm really trying to be better about it. I hope you don't think too poorly of me for that... I'm really trying to keep it under control. Does that help answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
